headline: Quantum Protocols, Cryptanalysis, and Molecular Dynamics
summary: Today's research spans diverse physical and computational domains, ranging from quantum cryptography and measurement-based frameworks to molecular topology and ion-trap noise. Several papers advance quantum security protocols and analysis tools, while others explore the fundamental intersections of quantum mechanics and chemical dynamics.

themes.title: Quantum Security and Cryptanalysis
themes.body: Recent advances in quantum security include unconditional proof for certifiable randomness protocols against shallow-query adversaries, and novel masked auto-correlation primitives coupled with quantum attack pipelines for symmetric-key cryptanalysis.

themes.title: Quantum Computation and Measurement Frameworks
themes.body: New tools for quantum platforms include Graphix, a Python framework for measurement-based quantum computation, alongside a randomized single-copy measurement method for certifying quantum fidelity susceptibility.

themes.title: Molecular Topology and Ion Trap Noise
themes.body: Work in physical chemistry explores how electronic topology impacts molecular conical intersections and chemical dynamics, while ion-trap physics research models geometry-controlled correlated electric-field noise.

connections.body: Both papers advance quantum protocol verification, focusing respectively on certifying fidelity susceptibility via randomized single-copy measurements and establishing unconditional security for certifiable randomness protocols.
